content: Mariana Reyes, representing the organization ¿Y yo, por qué no? (YYPN), contributed her expertise on HIV/AIDS in collaboration with UNAIDS. Enow Awah Georges Stevens, from the Organization for Health in Sustainable Development, and Lindsey Wise, from the World Food Programme, also provided significant input. Additional valuable suggestions were offered by Elsie Akwara from WHO's Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) department, Darryl Wade Barrett from WHO's Department of Health Systems and Innovation, Shelly Chadha from WHO's Noncommunicable Diseases (NCDs) division, and Julia Gorman from WHO's Department of Environment, Climate Change, and Health. Elizabeth Katwan and Sarah Keogh, both from WHO's Maternal, Child, and Adolescent Health (MCA) department, also contributed. Dzmitry Krupchanka, representing WHO's Department of Mental Health and Substance Use, and Yong Feng Liu from UNESCO, provided their insights. Wahyu Retno Mahanani, from WHO's Department for Data and Analytics, and Andrew Marsh, also from WHO's MCA department, added their expertise. Andreas Mueller and Roberta Ortiz Sequeira, both from WHO's NCDs division, and Natschja Nash-Mendez from WHO's Department of Digital Health and Innovation, were instrumental in shaping the discussions. Mervat Nessim, from WHO's Department for Health Promotion, Holly Newby from WHO's MCA department, Emma Pearce from WHO's NCDs division, and Leanne Riley, also from WHO's NCDs division, provided critical feedback. David Ross, an independent consultant, and Oscar San Roman from WHO's Regional Office for the Americas, contributed their perspectives. Benoit Varenne, from WHO's NCDs division, also played a key role. WHO extends its gratitude to all participants of the eight virtual consultation workshops on adolescent well-being held in 2021. These workshops informed the content of the second edition of the guidance. Additionally, WHO acknowledges the contributions of participants in the 2023 public consultations, which included youth consultations and discussions with policymakers and academia. These sessions provided valuable suggestions for refining the draft document. Administrative support for this initiative was provided by Gersende Moyse. The guidance document, titled Global Accelerated Action for the Health of Adolescents (AA-HA.), aims to assist governments in identifying national and strategic priorities for adolescent health. It emphasizes the importance of timely, equitable, integrated, lifelong, and efficient health services to ensure the well-being of adolescents.
